::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Part I · Clinical questions and data** · **Level:** entry · **Teaching units:** 01–04 (4 × 45 min) ·
**Required reading:** core readings of B01 and B03 (about 20 minutes) · **Lab:** [Lab W1](../exercises/lab-w1-case-table.qmd)
:::

## Guiding question

**How many independent observations do we actually have, and which question can they answer?**

After a fictitious wrist injury there is one radiograph, two readings and several measurements. Before anyone
fits a model, the team has to agree on what is being claimed, about whom, at what time and compared with what.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this workshop you can

1. formulate a descriptive, a prognostic and a causal question about the same material and name the decision each
   one would support;
2. state purpose, target population, reference standard, time zero and independent unit for a clinical question;
3. count people, images and readings in a table by hand and in R, and locate an identifier error and a unit error;
4. write a data dictionary with key, unit, time zero and reason for collection;
5. distinguish training data from application data for a rule and for a learnt threshold;
6. draw a data flow for care, research and teaching, and justify removing every field the teaching table does not
   need.

## Preparation

- **Required reading** (about 20 minutes):
  [B01 · Clinical decisions and the translational chain – core reading](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b01-clinical-decision.html#sec-b01-core)
  and
  [B03 · How data arise: missingness and denominators – core reading](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b03-how-data-arise.html#sec-b03-core).
- **Before the session:** install R (any version from 4.4) and, if you like, RStudio or Positron. Open
  [`r/w1-case-table.R`](../r/w1-case-table.R) once. If anything fails, bring the printed lab page; a partner
  computer is enough.
- **Bring:** paper and a pen. Unit 01 starts without a screen.

## The case

> A 52-year-old cyclist falls on an outstretched hand. In the emergency department the wrist is swollen and tender.
> A radiograph is taken and read twice: once by the emergency team, once by radiology. Two days later a follow-up
> image is taken. A research group wants to use such cases to develop a fracture alert; a lecturer wants to use them
> in a course.

Everything in the case and in the tables is *synthetic*. Any similarity to a real person is coincidental.

## Teaching units

| Unit | Task | Minutes | Observable evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 01 | Entry self-assessment (5 min, below). Trace the patient's pathway and the research question. Fix target, time point and addressee of a prediction. Formulate a descriptive, a prognostic and a causal question about the same material. | 45 | A case card with three question types, each with population, time zero and the decision it supports. |
| 02 | Count people, images and readings first by hand, then in R ([Lab W1, Parts A–B](../exercises/lab-w1-case-table.qmd)). Locate the identifier error and the unit error. | 45 | A data dictionary with key, unit, time zero and reason for collection; the three corrected counts. |
| 03 | Compare a fixed rule with a learnt threshold on a small table ([Part C](../exercises/lab-w1-case-table.qmd#part-c)). Mark training and application. | 45 | A sketch of both approaches and an R script that recreates the starting table in a fresh session. |
| 04 | Draw one data flow for care, research and teaching. Mark roles, expected benefit and dispensable fields. Build the reduced teaching table ([Part D](../exercises/lab-w1-case-table.qmd#part-d)). | 45 | A reduced teaching table and a reasoned decision to drop identifying free-text fields. |

### Entry self-assessment (unit 01, 5 minutes) {#self-assessment}

Rate each statement from 1 (not at all) to 5 (fully), anonymously. You will see the same statements again in W8.
The ratings are feedback for you and for the course team; they never count towards a grade.

1. I can tell which number is the denominator of a percentage in a clinical study.
2. I can explain why images from the same patient in training and test data are a problem.
3. I can check whether a cited source actually supports a sentence.
4. I know who has to be informed, and by when, if patient data reach the wrong recipient.

Then work on **short case A** for five minutes, on paper and without help:

> A research group reports "94% accuracy on 1,200 test images" for a model that classifies tissue in images from
> 20 fictitious rats. Images of every rat were used both for training and for testing. A week later a technician
> notices that a spreadsheet with the animal-house cage cards, including the names of the responsible staff, was
> sent to an external software helpdesk.
>
> (a) What is the independent number of units in the test? (b) What does the 94% measure? (c) Name the first two
> steps after the spreadsheet is discovered.

Keep your answer. The course team collects it anonymously and compares it with a parallel case in W8.

### Three question types (unit 01)

| Type | Example for the wrist case | Decision it supports | Comparison needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Descriptive | What share of adults presenting with wrist pain after a fall have a fracture on imaging? | Staffing of radiology in the emergency department | None; a well-defined population and denominator |
| Prognostic | Which patients will still have reduced grip strength after six weeks? | Who gets an early physiotherapy appointment | Predictors known at time zero, outcome later |
| Causal | Does an immediate second read of every radiograph reduce missed fractures? | Whether to introduce the second read | Patients with and without the second read, comparable at time zero |

- Tables: [raw export](../data/w1-register-raw.csv), [corrected table](../data/w1-register-corrected.csv),

## Four perspectives in this workshop

- **Ethics.** Who would act differently because of the alert, and who carries the harm of a wrong answer? The
  case card names one affected person.
- **Regulation.** Only indirectly: the intended purpose of a future alert decides which rules apply. This becomes
  the central question in [W7](w7-regulation-data-protection-incident.qmd).
- **Data protection.** The data flow in unit 04 separates care, research and teaching. Free text and exact age are
  removed because the teaching question does not need them (data minimisation, Article 5(1)(c) of the
  [General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)).
- **Security.** A teaching table that leaves the clinic is a copy that has to be protected or, better, that
  contains nothing worth protecting.

## Transition to W2

The case card and the data dictionary are the first two parts of your project. In W2 you add an evidence card: a
claim about your case, checked against its original source.
